messages:
Samir (eng-ml): Heads up — getting multiple customer reports of 502/504s on hosted inference since 09:12 UTC. Grafana shows gateway 5xx spike starting ~09:10. Traces point at prefix-cache redis errors. @Tabitha
Lina (infra): I see the alert too. redis-proxy-3 logs: \"TLS handshake failed: EOF\" repeated, then \"connection refused\". Frontend traces show upstream read_timeouts + conn resets. Link: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/redis-proxy/redis-proxy-overview
infra-bot: [ALERT] prod/redis-proxy group >95% conn usage on redis-proxy-2/3/4 — 502s increasing (rule: redis.proxy.conn_limit).
Tabitha (oncall): Pinging SRE/infra. Quick triage: is this auth/TLS cert expiry or traffic spike causing conn pool exhaustion? Any recent rollouts?
Alex (support): Multiple customers opened tickets with traces and example requests. Repro steps I used: 
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' \
  -d '{"model":"longseq-v2","input":"hello"}'
```
Response from gateway: HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
Server: nginx
X-Upstream-Error: upstream read timeout

Maria (sre): quick check on Redis cluster metrics: spike in connection rejects and TLS handshake failures at 09:09. CPU on redis-proxy-3 jumped to 95%. `ss -s` shows many FIN_WAIT/TIME_WAIT. I'm seeing increased prefix miss rate starting ~09:00 — looks like cache key cardinality exploded.
Samir (eng-ml): We did rollout of longseq-v2 at 08:55 which increases sequence length and creates longer-lived KV entries (bigger prefix keys). Could be sudden increase in cache footprint and misses (cold start storm).
Lina (infra): Proposed short mitigations: 1) fail-open prefix cache for reads (use local LRU) 2) scale redis-proxy group + recycle redis-proxy-3 3) enable circuit breaker on gateway for backend errors. Applying (1) now — patching feature flag `prefix_cache.fail_open=true` to prod.
Tabitha (oncall): Please also add a temporary rule to route traffic away from redis-proxy-3 during restart: `kubectl cordon redis-proxy-3` equivalent in cluster manager. Do it one node at a time.
Ops: Doing a rolling restart of redis-proxy-3 now, scaling replicas from 3 -> 6 to absorb connection churn. ETA ~5m.
Alex (support): Noted — told CS to pause onboarding jobs for affected customers and posting status update. CS-Bot posted: \"We are investigating elevated errors impacting hosted inference for some customers. Engineering is triaging.\"
Lina (infra): Restart done on redis-proxy-3, scaled proxies to 6, and applied fail-open. TLS handshake error count dropped immediately. Gateway 5xxs fell from 12% -> 1.6% in last 10m.
Maria (sre): Rolling restart revealed expired intermediate cert on redis-proxy-3 (partial rotation failed during last deploy). Rotated cert, verified handshake. Also found client connection pool in frontends didn't backoff on repeated TLS errors causing connection storms — adding backpressure.
Samir (eng-ml): Root cause hypothesis: model rollout increased cache misses + larger keys => surge of new prefix lookups; one proxy had partial cert rotation fail => TLS failures + repeated reconnects => conn pool exhaustion => upstream timeouts/5xx.
Tabitha (oncall): Current mitigation status: fail-open enabled, redis-proxy restarted and cert rotated, proxies scaled. Monitoring for 30m. Will keep circuit breaker enabled at gateway at 10r/s per prefix for now.
Alex (support): Customer impact summary for CS: affected hostnames: hosted-api-prod region-us-east-1. Error types seen: 502/504, elevated p50/p95 latency. CS notified customers A, B, C and created SEV tickets.
Lina (infra): Postmortem action items being tracked: 
- ensure cert rotations are fully verified across replicas (automation)
- add graceful backoff + jitter in client conn pool on TLS/auth errors
- pre-warm/prefill prefix cache after model rollouts that change key cardinality
- add alert for sudden prefix miss rate increase + key cardinality delta
Tabitha (oncall): I'll open an incident in PagerDuty and start a postmortem doc. Tags: redis, tls, conn-exhaustion, cache-storm, rollout.
Samir (eng-ml): Short-term: revert longseq-v2 rollout for small customers if issues persist; long-term: add prefetching + local warm cache on deploys.
Maria (sre): Metrics stable for 12m, 5xx at baseline. Closing active escalation after 30m observation. Will follow up with full incident writeup.
CS-Bot: Update to customers sent at 10:05 UTC. 
Alex (support): Thanks all. Please flag if any customers continue to see errors. :thumbsup:
Tabitha (oncall): Thanks team — keeping channel open for 30m to watch, then will archive and link postmortem.
